newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper targets US$2,650, but selling looms.
newsitem.headline: LME copper targets US$2,650, but selling looms.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices are expected to take out the US$2,600 level later on Friday and take aim at $2,650, but such a rise is seen running into heavy selling, Far East base metal dealers said.
"It will try to regain $2,600," a senior dealer at a metal trading firm in Singapore said.
"Copper should not cross $2,600. If it crosses $2,600, it will attract heavy selling," Vinod Kumar, director of metal company Donald Mcarthy in Singapore, said.
LME copper came off a 13-month high on Thursday of $2,609 a tonne to end $19 higher on the day at $2,580 a tonne. Three-month copper was quoted by the trade at 0400 GMT at around $2,577/82 a tonne.
Metal broker Brandeis said in its daily review, copper found good support from short-covering during the afternoon session.
"Chartwise, a very good close with more gains likely as the moving averages rise in tandem, the next objective being $2,650 (a tonne), the top of the current trading channel," it said.
A Japanese trader said, however, that copper may be vulnerable to a mild correction.
"I feel copper should be going back to $2,550," he said.

Base metal dealers in the Far East said the ongoing strike at Inco's Sudbury operations in Canada and problems plaguing the Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea should provide some support for the red metal.
"Inco and Ok Tedi will underpin the market," one said.

South Korea's LG Metals said on Friday a 10,000-tonne shipment of copper concentrate for late-July delivery had been delayed, following on from news of a hold-up of an estimated 25,000 tonnes for Japan's Nippon Mining on Thursday.
Zinc prices are seen softening further after hitting 4-1/2 year highs over the past two weeks, dealers said.
"Zinc looks a bit soft," a trader said.
Brandeis said that although "support at $1,355 managed to hold, the chart picture indicates a loss of upwards momentum."
Support for zinc will be seen "at $1,340 and then $1,320, with resistance at $1,375 (a tonne)," it added.
Three month zinc was quoted by regional dealers at 0400 GMT at $1,356/59 a tonne, slightly easier from the close on the LME of $1,359.
